formulas.title: Punnett Square Probability
formulas.eq: F = probability of a specific offspring genotype = product of parental allele probabilities
formulas.note: For independent traits, multiply probabilities of each trait's outcome (product rule); for either/or outcomes, add probabilities (sum rule). A dihybrid cross of AaBb × AaBb gives 9:3:3:1 phenotype ratio.

formulas.title: Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit Test
formulas.worked: Example: 3:1 ratio expected in 100 offspring → Expected = 75:25. Observed = 80:20 → χ² = (5²/75)+(5²/25) = 0.33+1.0 = 1.33
formulas.note: Compare the calculated χ² to a critical value table using degrees of freedom (categories − 1). A low χ² (below the critical value) supports the hypothesized ratio; p > 0.05 means no significant deviation.

formulas.title: Recombination Frequency
formulas.eq: RF (%) = (number of recombinant offspring ÷ total offspring) × 100
formulas.worked: Example: 18 recombinants out of 200 total offspring → RF = 18/200 × 100 = 9%
formulas.note: 1% recombination frequency ≈ 1 map unit (centimorgan, cM). Genes with RF close to 50% assort independently (unlinked or very far apart); RF near 0% indicates tight linkage.

formulas.title: Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium
formulas.worked: If q² (aa frequency) = 0.01, then q = 0.1, p = 0.9. Carrier frequency (2pq) = 2 × 0.9 × 0.1 = 0.18 (18%)
formulas.note: p = frequency of the dominant allele, q = frequency of the recessive allele. Used to estimate carrier frequency for recessive diseases from the frequency of affected individuals in a population.

formulas.title: Pedigree / Bayesian Recurrence Risk
formulas.eq: Posterior odds = Prior odds × Conditional (test) odds
formulas.worked: Example: Prior risk of being a carrier = 1/2. If a test is 90% sensitive and comes back negative, conditional odds favor non-carrier 9:1 → posterior odds = (1/2 × 1) : (1/2 × 0.1) = 5:0.05 = 100:1 against carrier
formulas.note: Convert prior risk to odds, multiply by conditional probabilities from test results or unaffected relatives, then convert back to a probability: P = odds ÷ (odds + 1).

formulas.title: Autosomal Recessive Recurrence Risk
formulas.eq: Two carrier parents (Aa × Aa): risk to each child = 1/4 affected, 1/2 carrier, 1/4 unaffected non-carrier
formulas.worked: If both parents are known carriers: P(affected child) = 1/4 = 25%
formulas.note: For an unaffected sibling of an affected child, P(carrier | unaffected) = 2/3, since the 1/4 homozygous-dominant possibility is excluded.

formulas.title: X-Linked Recessive Recurrence Risk
formulas.eq: Carrier mother (XᴸX) × unaffected father (XY): sons 1/2 affected, daughters 1/2 carriers
formulas.worked: P(affected son) = 1/2 × 1/2 (being male) = 1/4 of all children
formulas.note: All daughters of an affected father and unaffected mother become obligate carriers, since fathers pass their only X to every daughter.

formulas.title: Mean, Variance & Standard Deviation
formulas.eq: Mean (μ) = Σx ÷ n | Variance (σ²) = Σ(x−μ)² ÷ n | SD (σ) = √Variance
formulas.note: Standard deviation describes how spread out data is around the mean; used to describe variability in trait measurements or lab values.

formulas.title: Standard Error & Confidence Interval
formulas.note: A narrower confidence interval reflects a larger, more precise sample. SE shrinks as sample size grows, even though SD itself does not.

formulas.title: Correlation Coefficient (r)
formulas.worked: r ranges from −1 to +1: r = +1 perfect positive correlation, r = −1 perfect negative correlation, r = 0 no linear correlation
formulas.note: In genetics, r is used e.g. to compare trait values between relatives (parent-offspring correlation) as part of heritability estimation.

formulas.title: Heritability Estimate (Twin Method)
formulas.note: H² close to 1 suggests strong genetic contribution; H² close to 0 suggests environment dominates. MZ = monozygotic (identical), DZ = dizygotic (fraternal) twins.

formulas.title: Odds Ratio & Relative Risk
formulas.worked: 2×2 table: a=exposed+disease, b=exposed+no disease, c=unexposed+disease, d=unexposed+no disease
formulas.note: OR > 1 suggests increased risk with exposure; used in case-control genetic association studies where true incidence is unknown.
